clusters.mechanism: Sticky-implementer invalidation relies on the in-memory changedCells set, which is empty after operator reset and daemon restart, so a removed saved implementer is appended and pinned again.
changedCells is never cleared, so after any historical edit, preferred implementers outside the edited cell (including escalated ones) are permanently discarded.
RuntimePolicy constructor revalidates persisted operator cells and prefer rows against the current catalog and throws, so a stale row prevents daemon startup with no CLI/API recovery.
policyRevision is a single global abort signal triggered by every routing edit, so unrelated queued or pending invocations are aborted and rerouted, losing their queue positions.
Validation errors wrap String(error) from zod, producing raw JSON issue dumps that are hard to read.
A pre-existing config-cache test fails on both base and HEAD, unrelated to the change.
Factory.policy now returns the effective policy including operator overrides, so the eval policy diff against the proposed overlay is misleading.
Resetting a cell with no existing override still writes a null-to-null history row and publishes an SSE change.
Documentation claims provider cards appear only on the Providers page, but the Models page still renders them.
